summary: Moderate early blight detected on tomato. Timely fungicide application and leaf removal should control spread.

sections.title: What this means
sections.body: Early blight is a fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani, common in warm, humid conditions. Moderate severity indicates visible lesions on multiple leaves but limited spread to stems or fruit so far.

sections.title: Recommended actions
sections.body: Remove and destroy affected lower leaves. Apply a labeled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or copper-based) following local guidance. Improve airflow by spacing plants and avoid overhead watering.

citations.title: Early Blight of Tomato and Potato
citations.snippet: Early blight severity is best managed through cultural controls combined with timely fungicide rotation.

safety_notice: This guidance is generated from retrieved agricultural sources and does not replace an expert. Always follow local label instructions for any treatment.
